component.name: Grab
component.summary: A GNOME download manager with pause, resume and history

description.p: Queue, pause, resume and monitor file downloads with smart auto-resume, in a native GNOME interface.
A few optional capabilities are not granted by default; enable the ones you need with "flatpak override":

ul.li: Save downloads to a custom folder outside Downloads: flatpak override --user --filesystem=/path/to/folder io.github.houssemko.Grab

screenshot.caption: Empty state with a New Download shortcut
Active downloads with per-block progress maps

description.p: Fix: a preset GSettings schema path that lacks this app's schema no longer aborts startup — it is ignored in favor of the app's own install tree.
Fix: the portable tarball no longer aborts on startup — the binary finds its GSettings schemas in its own install prefix, and the tarball ships compiled schemas.
Fix: the header search toggle is hidden when the queue is empty, and an open search bar collapses with the last entry.
New: GNOME HIG search pattern — a header-bar toggle reveals a search bar with the status filter alongside. Open it with the button, by typing, or with Ctrl+F.
Stability: removed per-download custom headers in favor of automatic headers. Internal code cleanups.

New: task search and status filter, multi-URL batch add, task rename. Torrent: upload stats on rows, custom trackers, seed ratio and time limits, listen port. Downloads: per-download custom headers, keep-server-file-date option, command-line URL enqueue.
Hardening: torrent archive handling is confined to the app data dir, duplicate settings key removed, peer-limit edge case fixed.
Fix: About dialog no longer crashes; release notes are embedded in the app.
Dialog improvements: access keys on action buttons, clearer file-chooser labels, About page with release notes, Enter key confirms dialogs. Dependency updates.
Fix: URL apply tick returns after failed validation so over-long URLs can be corrected and retried.
Full interface translation support (gettext); typed settings access throughout.
Fix: finished torrents are evicted from the session, stopping RAM growth; leaner per-tick updates; refreshed screenshots.
Refreshed AppData screenshots: block maps and the new preferences pages.
Per-block download map: click a downloading row to reveal downloaded blocks; HIG separator between progress bar and blocks.
Torrent delete moves the real download folder to Trash; magnets download into their own subfolder; file-picker leftovers are cleaned at finish; peer limit defaults to unlimited.
Fix: finished torrent downloads keep their .torrent file so deleting them moves the real download folder to Trash.
Fix: deleting a torrent download now moves the real download folder to Trash, and re-adding a torrent right after deleting it no longer fails with a phantom already-in-queue error.
Change: the torrent file picker no longer remembers past selections, opening a .torrent file shows the same file list as the picker, and downloading rows show how many files are selected.
New: the torrent file picker remembers your per-file selection, so re-adding the same torrent pre-checks your last choice.
Maintenance: regression coverage for per-file torrent selection. No user-facing changes.
Fix: re-adding an already-queued torrent with a different file selection now fails fast instead of silently adopting the wrong files. Grab no longer claims to be a web browser.
Fix: per-file torrent selection now survives app restarts instead of silently downloading everything.
Code cleanup: removed dead code and merged duplicate helpers. No behavior changes.

Torrent support: magnet links and .torrent files with a file picker, multi-file torrents in their own folder, a dedicated Torrent preferences page, and network settings on their own page. Removing a torrent keeps partial files so Undo resumes instead of restarting.
Security hardening: download folders must be absolute paths, URLs with embedded credentials are rejected, fresh downloads claim their destination atomically, and redirects are capped at five hops.
Main thread never blocks on portal or file I/O (async bus lookups, worker-thread list imports), and diagnostics move to structured tracing logs.
Fixes the suspend block never engaging (portal flags are positional), plus duplicate-request fencing and diagnostic logging.
Release bundles now build clean in CI and attach automatically; test bundles build on demand and on packaging pull requests. Distribution is Flatpak-only.
Adaptive piece sizing for huge files, stall hardening, cross-desktop sleep inhibit with toggle, background portal support, and Flatpak-only distribution.
Hardened downloads: verified sizes, resumable retries, healing server changes, per-row retry, and a full review pass over engine and interface.
Queue-for-later button, auto-park when lowering simultaneous downloads, no more phantom failures or flickering progress on re-queued rows.
Finished-download notifications show just the filename.
Cancelled downloads no longer raise the failure banner; Cancel All is a single pass with no stray background tasks.
Cancel All now asks for confirmation first; background notification simplified to a single line.
First stable release: segmented downloads with smart auto-resume, pause/resume, download history, live preferences, and a native HIG-compliant interface.
First beta: native HTTP backend with pause/resume, segmented downloads, download history, and HIG-compliant UI.
Security hardening: capped split sizes, failed engine tasks report instead of stalling, stricter filenames.
Progress rows show downloaded-of-total amounts; background notice only while transferring.
Download speed measures new bytes only, so resumed downloads read correctly.
Segmented downloads resume across restarts instead of starting over.
Survives killed segmented downloads without corrupting files; leaner engine and test helpers.
Survives throttling hosts by dropping to one stream; fixes segmented resume corrupting finished files.
Downloads take the server-advertised filename, so video links save with the right extension.
Finished downloads show their final size where the speed was.
URL length limit, CI checks on every push, and contributor documentation.
New Download keeps its pill shape but sizes to its text instead of stretching full-width.
Smaller New Download button; header add button only shows alongside the download list.
HIG compliance pass: failure banner, undo for removals, keyboard shortcuts, screen-reader labels, and release hardening.
Native HTTP backend with pause/resume, background downloads, and download history.
Initial release.
